title: Senior's toolkit: talking to an identity provider
summary: Read a discovery document, get a client-credentials token with curl, make a PKCE pair with openssl, and configure AddOpenIdConnect.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: talking to an identity provider
steps.body: OAuth and OpenID Connect problems are solved by looking at the real HTTP: what the provider publishes, what you sent, what came back. These are the commands and settings experienced developers use with Entra ID, Auth0, Okta or Keycloak.

toolkit.what: Every OpenID provider publishes its endpoints, signing keys location and supported features here. Read it before configuring anything.
flags: must match the `iss` in tokens exactly, trailing slash included
where the public signing keys are

toolkit.what: Get a token for a service (no user) straight from the token endpoint. The quickest way to see whether a client id, secret and scope are right.
flags: send the client credentials as HTTP Basic
what the token is for; on Entra it is `api://<app>/.default`

toolkit.what: Make a PKCE pair by hand to test an authorization-code flow: a random `code_verifier`, and its SHA-256 in base64url as the `code_challenge`.
flags: raw SHA-256 bytes of the verifier
toolkit.example:
v=$(openssl rand -base64 48 | tr '+/' '-_' | tr -d '=\n')
c=$(printf %s "$v" | openssl dgst -sha256 -binary | openssl base64 -A | tr '+/' '-_' | tr -d '=')

toolkit.what: Sign users in to a server-rendered ASP.NET Core app with an OpenID provider, using the authorization-code flow with PKCE, and keep the session in a cookie.
flags: the issuer URL; metadata is read from its discovery document
on by default; keep it on
keep claim names as the provider sent them (`sub`, not a long URI)

toolkit.what: Watch the redirect dance: the authorize request, the callback with `code` and `state`, and any `error=` the provider returns. Without Preserve log the redirects wipe the list.
toolkit.example: F12 > Network > Preserve log > sign in > click /signin-oidc

steps.prompt: Match each discovery document field to what it is for.
pairs: must equal the `iss` claim in tokens
where the API fetches public signing keys
where codes and client credentials are exchanged for tokens
where the browser is sent to sign in

steps.prompt: Users sometimes land on an error page after signing in. The app log shows this while handling `/signin-oidc`. What is the likely cause?
code: error_description: 'AADSTS54005: OAuth2 Authorization code was already redeemed, please retry with a new valid code or use an existing refresh token.'
options: The authorization code was used twice, for example a retried or refreshed callback; codes are single-use, so restart the sign-in
The user typed the wrong password
steps.explain: `invalid_grant` means the code (or refresh token) is not acceptable: already used, expired, issued to another client, or the PKCE verifier or redirect URI does not match the original request. The `error_description` tells you which.

steps.prompt: Get a service token with the client credentials flow.
Put the steps of the authorization-code flow with PKCE in order, as you would see them in the Network tab.
lines: The app makes a code_verifier and sends its SHA-256 as code_challenge to /authorize
The user signs in at the provider
The provider redirects to /signin-oidc with code and state
The app checks state, then POSTs code and code_verifier to the token endpoint
The provider returns the id_token and access_token

steps.prompt: After sign-in, `User.FindFirst("sub")` is null, although jwt.ms shows a `sub` claim in the id token. What is the fix?
options: Set `MapInboundClaims = false`; by default `sub` is renamed to the long `nameidentifier` claim type URI
steps.explain: The handler maps short JWT claim names to old WS-Federation URIs unless told not to. Turning mapping off makes the claims in code match what you see in the token.

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Before configuring a new provider, read its discovery document; when a flow fails, open the Network tab with Preserve log and read the `error` and `error_description` the provider sent. Test service credentials with one curl call before writing any code.
